description: Named SQL source from an H3 dataset query.

name.description: Logical source name exposed to SQL widgets via {{name}}.

endpoint.description: Query endpoint speaking the /h3/query parameters: a full URL or a path relative to the current server root. Defaults to /h3/query. The viewer's token is sent only to the client's own server. Accepts a $param reference.

path.description: Indexed H3 dataset location (as listed by GET /h3/datasets). Accepts a $param reference.

cell.description: Spatial selector: an H3 cell id as a hex string; rows filed under it or its descendants.

minLng.description: Spatial selector: bounding box west edge.

minLat.description: Spatial selector: bounding box south edge.

maxLng.description: Spatial selector: bounding box east edge.

maxLat.description: Spatial selector: bounding box north edge.

hexMin.description: Spatial selector: raw H3 cell-id range start (hex string).

hexMax.description: Spatial selector: raw H3 cell-id range end (hex string).

timeMin.description: Inclusive ISO datetime; start of the time window.

timeMax.description: Inclusive ISO datetime; end of the time window.

dateMin.description: Alias of timeMin, as fused-hex sources name it.

dateMax.description: Alias of timeMax, as fused-hex sources name it.

columns.description: Columns to return; omitted means every column. An array, a comma-separated string, or a $param reference.

variables.description: Alias of columns, as fused-hex sources name it.

partition.description: Partition filter, keyed by partition column: {"scenario": ["ssp245", "ssp585"], "date": "2050-01"}.

partitionRange.description: Partition range filter, keyed by partition column: {"date": ["2050-01", "2050-06"]}; null for an open end.

maxRowGroups.description: Most row groups the server reads per page (server default 1024, max 4096).

maxPages.description: Most pages the widget follows before giving up. Defaults to 16; every page is held in browser memory.

loader.description: How the rows are read. server (the default) has the server read the row groups and answer Parquet pages. browser reads the row groups from object storage in the browser, from a plan the server answers (format=browser), trimmed to the query there; it needs the client's own server, a signed-in viewer and an execution environment, and fails otherwise. auto tries browser and falls back to server when the plan is refused or the browser loader cannot start.
